sourcePolicy: Prefer historical primary evidence; use current official rules only for unchanged general mechanics; mark community adaptations explicitly.

sources.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG Rulebook
sources.goatTreatment: Use general mechanics only; exclude modern mechanics and modern rule changes from the GOAT layer.

sources.title: Fast Effect Timing
sources.goatTreatment: Use the chart as the baseline and add GOAT Ignition Effect priority after a successful Summon or Chain resolution.

sources.title: Damage Step Rules
sources.goatTreatment: Use the sequence as a general scaffold; GOAT-specific activation restrictions and six substeps come from GoatFormat.com.

sources.title: Problem-Solving Card Text
sources.goatTreatment: Diagnostic vocabulary only. GOAT cards did not use PSCT, so old text and card-specific rulings remain authoritative.

sources.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Neuron TCG Card Database and Rule Search
sources.goatTreatment: Lookup aid only; do not overwrite the historical text, banlist or ruling snapshot.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — Rules & Policies
sources.goatTreatment: Primary community reference for the project's GOAT rules layer, while preserving its distinction from Konami's current rules.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — Basic Mechanics
sources.goatTreatment: Canonical GOAT adaptation for the listed differences; card-specific pages still win over a broad summary.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — 6 Facts That You Should Know About Priority
sources.goatTreatment: Use as the player-facing explanation of the historical priority layer; never let the bot use priority as a card property.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — Individual Card Rulings
sources.published: 2005 evidence curated by the Judge Corps; site footer 2015
sources.goatTreatment: Required lookup for a named card interaction. Never replace a CARD_SPECIFIC ruling with a generic modern rule.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — Ruling Notices
sources.goatTreatment: Use only after checking historical evidence; record the notice as a community adjudication, not as a 2005 primary document.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — Who's Winning? Goat Format Fundamentals
sources.goatTreatment: Adapted into decision features; it is strategic theory, not a legal ruling.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — Risk in Goat Format
sources.goatTreatment: Adapted into context-sensitive risk tolerance; never hard-code 'always be conservative'.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — The Philosophy of Greed
sources.goatTreatment: Adapted as a valuation model, not a deterministic rule.

sources.title: GoatFormat.com — The Science of Sideboarding Part 1
sources.goatTreatment: Use for the optional match/side-deck layer; it does not change single-duel rules.

sources.title: Goat World — Goat Format Rules: Complete Guide
sources.goatTreatment: Secondary cross-check; cannot overrule GoatFormat.com or historical evidence.

sources.title: ygopro-core issue: one chain per Damage Step substep
sources.goatTreatment: Comparison only. OCGCore and project tests remain authoritative for runtime behavior.
